subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic browser OAuth as an onboarding/auth method, and what consent, scope, billing/account-detection, token-storage, and fallback contract is acceptable?
rationale: Current main has provider seams and existing auth paths, but choosing to collect and refresh Anthropic OAuth credentials in onboarding crosses product UX, provider policy, and security boundaries that code inspection cannot settle.

options.title: Add provider-owned OAuth after approval
options.body: Expose a new Anthropic auth method through the plugin once maintainers approve scopes, callback behavior, token storage, refresh, docs, and upgrade/fallback handling.

options.title: Keep current explicit auth paths
options.body: Leave API-key, setup-token, and Claude CLI onboarding as the supported Anthropic paths and improve documentation or labels instead of adding browser OAuth now.

options.title: Prototype behind an experimental path
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned experimental OAuth flow only if it is clearly opt-in and does not replace existing Anthropic setup choices.

recommendation.title: Add provider-owned OAuth after approval
recommendation.body: Expose a new Anthropic auth method through the plugin once maintainers approve scopes, callback behavior, token storage, refresh, docs, and upgrade/fallback handling.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal on Anthropic auth and Claude CLI migration behavior closest to this request.
